There is also a diagonal line from the lower left to the upper right in the figure, and the question stem states that this diagonal line is a meridian. Then reason: When a river crosses contour lines, the curved tips of the contour lines at the valley usually point upstream. Therefore, the tips point to the left side of the figure, indicating that the left side of the figure is upstream and the right side of the figure is downstream, so the river should flow from left to right. Also because the diagonal line from lower left to upper right is a meridian, the upper-right direction can be regarded as north and the lower-left direction as south; under this orientation, the left side of the figure corresponds to the southwest direction, and the right side of the figure corresponds to the northeast direction. Therefore, river L may flow from southwest to northeast.
